doc.title: Skitch Henderson interviewed by Monk Rowe, New Milford, Connecticut, October 31, 1998

title: The Silo cooking school and tractors
summary: Ruth's cooking school at The Silo, his tractors and the barn home.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Talking about my children and grandchildren

blocks.x: I’m so pleased you’ve been able to find us a little time in your schedule. I just wanted to ask you about this whole wonderful home you have here, and The Silo. It started as a small idea and kind of grew into your cooking school?
Well that’s not me that’s my wife.

She carries the brain factory. I carry the travel factory. No I was in the racecar business at one time and one of our dear friends was a Grand Prix driver, as many of them, was killed. And his wife and Ruth started a little shop here. And then Louise decided this wasn’t a life for her so Ruth took it over and that was 25 years ago. And of course it’s grown like topsy, it’s fantastic what she’s done, and all the superstars of the cooking world come here to teach, which to me is the greatest accolade, because that’s for her really that they come. You know, Pepin, everybody comes here. And we live in a barn. My tractors were here when I moved here. This was the tractor barn.
You have an affinity for tractors also.
We saw like a steam driven tractor.
Yeah, the steamer is sitting out here, yeah, I have boiler problems, so I’ll get that fixed. But I have to get off the road to do it.
